source.title: Misalignment Has a Personality: A Big Five Account of Emergent Misalignment

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether emergent-misalignment data and fine-tuning share a personality signature, a conceptual test of V5. It measures Big Five profiles rather than rates of harmful or misaligned answers.
record.gate_note: The paper reports no rate of misaligned free-form answers on neutral prompts. Its fine-tuning readouts measure Big Five expression, not the harmful-answer behavior named in V1 or V2. Calibration, BIG5-CHAT transfer, and activation-steering validity results are not rows because they do not measure the emergent-misalignment mechanism or behavior in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study never measures misaligned free-form answers or harmful-answer rates. It takes Chen et al.'s misaligned corpora as given and projects data and fine-tuned models' neutral-question outputs onto Big Five vectors. That is a related construct, a personality profile, not the behaviour. It also never tests whether a direction mediates misalignment: the authors say they show 'measurement, correlation, and imprinting, not intervention', and steering was done only on base models. So its results do not bear on whether any version holds, V5 included. The findings go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that misalignment behaves like a personality shift: misaligned corpora share a low-A/low-C/high-E/high-N Big Five signature, and fine-tuning imprints it in generations and activations. Sycophancy reads as high extraversion and low conscientiousness rather than agreeableness. They state the evidence is measurement, correlation and imprinting, not intervention, and leave causal mediation to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Rather than testing the original narrow-task intervention with a harmful-answer rate, the paper reads Big Five projections from eight paired data categories and from selected LoRA-fine-tuned models' neutral-question generations and activations.
record.method_sensitivity: The profile and its magnitude vary by category and model; the authors report that re-reading across layers 16–24 leaves their conclusions unchanged. Fine-tuning readouts use a matched normal-split adapter as control.

fits_no_version.finding: Misaligned training corpora across eight categories share a Big Five shift: low A and C, high E and N. The two models' signatures correlate at r=0.94, and PC1 explains 91% (Qwen) and 72% (Llama) of variance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emergent-misalignment training data carry a shared, human-interpretable personality signature (low agreeableness and conscientiousness, high extraversion and neuroticism).

fits_no_version.finding: LoRA fine-tuning on misaligned versus matched normal splits shifts neutral-question generations along the data signature (r=0.83, about half magnitude). It also shifts activations on identical teacher-forced tokens (r=0.69). A text-judge readout agrees (r=0.90 with projection).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow misaligned fine-tuning imprints a broad personality shift (antagonism–disinhibition) on unrelated prompts, in behaviour and representations.

fits_no_version.finding: The misalignment axis is nearly orthogonal to the instruct-minus-base assistant axis (cos −0.25 Qwen, +0.10 Llama).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The misalignment personality direction is not the assistant persona reversed.

record.problems: Only two 7–8B models, English, and one fine-tuning method are studied. The outcomes are personality scores rather than harmful-answer rates; causal mediation is not tested. Some readouts reuse the extraction judge, and the Llama checkpoint has additional distillation and RL post-training.
record.rows_left_out: Calibration, BIG5-CHAT transfer, manipulation-based activation steering, assistant-persona comparison, and layer-depth results were left out because they do not measure the shared emergent-misalignment signature or misaligned-answer behavior named by the versions.

untested.parts: No misaligned free-form answer rates after insecure-code fine-tuning. Insecure code appears only as a data-corpus personality readout.
Fine-tunes on evil, medical-mistake and sycophancy data, but reports only Big Five shifts, no misaligned-answer rates.
No test that a direction mediates misaligned answers. Steering was on base models for trait validity only; ablation or steering on fine-tuned checkpoints is left to future work.
No size, seed or coherence-filter robustness or training time course of misalignment rates. One seed (0).

missing.what: Text-judge Big Five readout of fine-tuned generations (agreeableness d=−3.4, conscientiousness d=−3.0 pooled; r=0.70 with data signature)
Assistant-persona axis orthogonality to the misalignment axis
Length and sentiment confound controls on the fine-tuning shift (0.80× magnitude retained)

record.verdict_notes: Gate: the study measures personality projections, never a misaligned-answer rate, and does no mediation test on fine-tuned models. So no version is tested and the reader's V5 labels are dropped. Its 'insecure code' category is Chen et al.'s persona-vector data split, not Betley et al.'s fine-tune. The Llama checkpoint has extra distillation and RL post-training. Only one seed was used.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure insecure-code fine-tuning on unsuspecting-user data or harmful free-form answers against base and matched benign controls.
Measures personality shifts associated with several misaligned data categories, but not the predicted misaligned-answer rate after fine-tuning those datasets.
No reinforcement-learning intervention or reward-hack training.
Measures shared personality-profile associations, not whether a linear feature causally mediates misaligned answers or whether intervening on it changes those answers.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining mitigation test.
Reports two model sizes and robustness of personality-profile results, not the size, seed robustness, coherence-filter robustness, or training-time course of misaligned-answer rates.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Across the reported misaligned-data categories and two models
reader_labels.reason: A common Big Five profile appears in most categories; the two signature matrices correlate at r = 0.94, and fine-tuning shifts neutral-generation and representation profiles in the same general direction (rows r1-r17 and r20-r31). This supports a shared signature, not causal mediation.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Category-specific profiles and the causal-mediation interpretation
reader_labels.reason: Some category profiles depart from the shared pattern, PC1 explains 91% for Qwen but 72% for Llama, and the paper explicitly reports measurement and correlation rather than intervention on the fine-tuned checkpoints; this does not establish a single causal mediator (rows r3-r5, r11-r13, r16, r18-r19).
